speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're limping and feeling pain. Can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and what makes it better or worse? Also, have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Since the pain is referred to the knee but often originates higher up in children, does the pain ever seem to start in your left hip or groin, and is it worse in the morning? Also, can you show me exactly where it hurts when I press on the area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE). Although the pain is localized to the knee, this is a classic presentation of SCFE in a 7-year-old where hip pathology refers pain distally. Given your age and symptoms, this is an orthopedic emergency that requires immediate evaluation to prevent further slippage and avascular necrosis. I am authorizing the imaging team to proceed with an AP and lateral view of the left hip immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Left_Hip_XRay.
